_comment: The pre-registration of agent_architecture.md §7's last reporting rule: budget
and hyperparameters are fixed before any test run, all method debugging happens
on train, and every arm is reported on test — never 'best of'. Committed before
the registered search and before any test rollout; its sha256 travels with every
run (harness/preregistration.py), so an edit after the fact moves the hash rather
than quietly redefining what was promised. Amendments are appended to
'amendments' with their reason, never applied by rewriting a value in place.

commit_note: The tip carrying the repaired suite, the fixed metaprompt, T140's leakage check
and the glm-5.3 pin. This registration lands in the ONE commit after it and no
rollout of it exists against either, which is what registrations 2, 3 and 4 each
did and for the same reason: a registration cannot carry the hash of the commit
case_files_note: THE FIRST REGISTRATION ON THE REPAIRED SUITE. train and test_seen are new;
test_unseen is byte-identical to registrations 1-4, so it is the one split whose
figures may be read across the repair. `just cases-check` reports all three
byte-identical to a fresh generation pass.

a_strong_teacher_for_a_weak_student: THE CONFIGURATION PROMPT OPTIMIZATION IS USUALLY CLAIMED FOR, and the one no
registration has yet tested. Registrations 2 and 3 ran one model in both roles
and had to declare it a deviation from §5; registration 4 made them distinct but
left the proposer a small fast model.
Registration 4's proposer is what motivates the change rather than a preference
for a bigger model: deepseek-v4-flash wrote a `measurements` table with columns
such table or column exists, the tables being outflow/radiation/swc/tsoil/wetter
— and instructed the assistant to pass SQL to a sub-agent that takes natural
language. That candidate WON carrying the fabrication. A stronger proposer is
being asked to stop inventing the schema; whether it does is measured, not
glm-5.3 is NOT a dated snapshot, unlike deepseek-v4-flash-0731 and
ministral-8b-2512. §5's pin for it therefore rests on the canary alone, which is
the weaker of the two mechanisms and is recorded here as a known cost.
why_a_whitelist_is_still_a_pin: Unchanged in mechanism from registration 4, one slug wider. The pin is
process-wide and the run spans three models that share no provider, so
`allow_fallbacks: False` is held over a three-member whitelist whose
intersection with each model's provider set is a SINGLETON — verified live
against OpenRouter's endpoint listing on every `check_pins` run, which FAILS on
a whitelist it cannot verify or one whose intersection has two members.
glm-5.3 has exactly one server (`z-ai`, fp8), so it adds no routing freedom at
all: for this model the whitelist is not even a choice.

budget.available_note: Derived: registration 4's 18.0 less its own ledger (2.85). The repository's arithmetic, not a balance read from the provider.

basis: The student's cost is measured: registration 4 spent $0.00136 per rollout at
~11,900 tokens, so 2000 search rollouts ≈ $2.7 and the measurement's 1686 ≈
The PROPOSER's cost is an estimate and the largest unknown here. glm-5.3 bills
$1.40/$4.40 per Mtok against deepseek's $0.112/$0.224 — roughly 12x and 20x —
and is called once per reflection rather than once per rollout, so ~22
iterations at a metaprompt plus three examples is estimated at ~$0.5 and could
plausibly be double that. The limit is 10.0 rather than the estimate for
exactly this reason: this is the first run on this model and its reflection
cost has never been measured here.
The ledger prices every rollout at the .env rates (0.112/0.224) regardless of
which model served it, so its figures are internally consistent and are not
the invoice — the same caveat registration 4 carried, now larger because three
models with three price points share one table.

budget.if_exhausted: The split order in `measurement.splits` decides what is lost, as it has since registration 1's amendment 3. Registered before any test rollout and on no test number.

baseline: The weakened seed at the pinned candidate_prompt_versions, answered by
ministral-8b-2512 on the REPAIRED suite. Registered once and read twice, so the
reference arm and the search's seed cannot drift apart.
It is a deliberately degraded prompt on a deliberately small model and its
absolute scores are NEVER quoted as the assistant's performance.
It carries T107's known defect unchanged and registered in advance, as every
registration since the first has: T17a enters at 0.50 abstention accuracy,
failing 3/3 with correct reasoning and a wrong contract encoding, and T107 left
it for the search because the encoding lives in the optimizable text. A
candidate that repairs it is measuring what the thesis claims to measure, and
this sentence exists so the improvement cannot later be read as a baseline
quietly weakened to make room for it. On this student it compounds with a
parse-failure rate registration 4 measured at 3.0% on train and 8.4% on
test_seen, which is a different failure of the same contract and is counted
It is NOT comparable with registration 4's baseline: same text, same model,
optimized: Whatever candidate the one registered search selects, starting from that seed
and proposed by glm-5.3. Not the best of several searches, not the best
iteration by test score, not a hand-picked candidate.
Registration 4's winner is NOT this arm and is not carried over. It was selected
against a different proposer on a different suite, and it is the candidate whose
memorized constant this registration exists partly to prevent.

why_2000: Registered on the starvation evidence and not on a result. A full valset
evaluation costs 100 rollouts, so registration 4's 500 bought six iterations —
improving at 1, 2 and 3, then nothing at 4, 5 and 6 before the budget ended.
2000 buys roughly 22, which is enough for a plateau to be visible AS a plateau
rather than inferred from three barren iterations.
It gives up comparability of the SEARCH with registrations 2-4, which all ran
500. That is the trade this registration accepts: the budget was one of the
things held fixed precisely so it could be moved once, deliberately, with the
llm_cache_hygiene: `.cache/llm` is CLEARED before the registered search, and clearing means
REMOVING THE DIRECTORY'S CONTENTS rather than deleting `cache.db`: the store is
sharded into subdirectories and a file delete leaves entries behind. The cache
key covers the model id, so a glm call cannot collide with a deepseek one, but
registration 4's ministral rollouts are the same model on the same prompts and

measurement.pairing: the identical committed cases, in file order, for every arm and every repeat
repeats_note: Three, unchanged since registration 2. The repeats ARE the replication and are
what makes the LLM cache's being off matter. Registration 4 measured the noise
floor on this student at 0.187 of test_seen cases disagreeing across their own
repeats in the baseline arm and 0.278 in the optimized one, against 0.135 on
deepseek — an 8B model bought its headroom with instability, and every
difference this run reports is read against that.
workers_note: NOT a registered parameter and deliberately so: it changes no request, no
result and no key. Registration 4 ran the measurement at `--workers 4` after
measuring ~62 s per case serially against T134's ~21 s, which projected to 29
hours. The cost is that `mean_latency_s` becomes a contended figure and stops
being comparable with a serial run's; every scored metric is unaffected. Stated
here so the diagnostic is read with it rather than against T134's.

why_it_is_not_widened: Registration 4 lost 57 and 59 of 375 test_seen rollouts and 82 and 78 of 168
test_unseen rollouts to `upstream`, nearly all cache misses on windows a
candidate chose. The counts CONVERGED between the arms, which is the property
§7 reads, so the neighbourhood is left alone.
The repaired suite redraws 36 train and 64 test_seen cases, so their windows are
new and the capture pass fills them before the search. Whether the miss rate
moves is a fact about the new draw and is reported, not predicted.
If the per-arm counts diverge, §7's repeat condition fires and this run is
repeated rather than reported — registered here, before the counts exist.

analysis.repeat_reduction: mean over the repeats per case, before any aggregation over cases
analysis.primary_estimand: the paired difference optimized - baseline, per metric, on test_seen
analysis.test_unseen_trajectory: per-template win/loss table; no accuracy and no interval
analysis.abstention: accuracy over the unanswerable cases and the false-abstention rate over the answerable ones, reported separately and never blended
analysis.exclusion: harness_error cases leave every aggregate and are counted per arm with their sources broken out; invalid_argument never excludes
parse_failure: Reported apart from answer accuracy and read BEFORE any other number, as in
registration 4. The contract block is preserved byte-for-byte so that a weakened
seed degrades routing and not format; registration 4 nevertheless measured 8.4%
in the baseline arm on test_seen, so on this student the contract's legibility
is part of what is being measured and a candidate that repairs it is credited
with improving format rather than reasoning.
answer_leakage: NEW IN THIS REGISTRATION, and the reason registration 4's headline number could
not be taken at face value. T140's check refuses a candidate carrying a gold
answer the seed did not contain: reported for the search, REFUSED for the
measurement unless the run declares itself exploratory. Any leak the search
reports is published beside the result whether or not the run proceeds, and a
measurement that runs `--exploratory` past a leak is never a test number.
The check is a floor and not a proof: it finds a value copied verbatim and not a
candidate that encodes an answer in words.
analysis.residual_nondeterminism: MEASURED, from the three repeats per condition. Every arm difference is read against it, and a difference smaller than it is within the noise floor rather than a small effect.
analysis.multiplicity: no correction across the four metrics. They are four declared quantities, not a family searched over for a winner.
card_recall_caveat: Registration 3's search found card_recall moving OPPOSITE to every other metric,
and registration 4's dropped it 0.950 → 0.900. The metric scores the union of
every lookup_reference call in a run, so an unselective agent scores higher and a
candidate that routes more deliberately can lose recall while improving. It
carries 0.1 of the selection weight and is reported with this caveat wherever it
per_template_decomposition: REQUIRED OF THIS RUN, not optional. Registration 4's aggregate was carried by two
templates of nineteen and its significance by one, which the aggregate alone did
not show. Every reported difference is published with its per-template breakdown
and with the effect of dropping the largest contributor, so a result resting on
one template is visible as one.
comparison_with_earlier_registrations: REPORTED SIDE BY SIDE, NEVER POOLED AND NEVER DIFFERENCED. Registrations 2 and 4
were measured on the pre-repair suite and this one is not, which is a harder
break than the model and prompt changes between them: the cases themselves
differ. test_unseen is the one split byte-identical across the repair.
What the runs carry jointly is a BRACKET on how much prompt optimization adds as
a function of the room the seed and the model leave — three or four points on
that surface, reported as such, never as one effect size with an interval.
what_a_null_would_mean: A null here is the strongest negative result this testbed can produce. The seed
has ~14 points of headroom on the blended score and ~21 on answer accuracy, the
proposer is a strong model distinct from the student, the budget is four times
the one that improved three times in six iterations, the suite no longer leaks
parameters between splits, and the metaprompt no longer invites copying the
oracle. If the optimizer cannot move a weak student under those conditions, the
remaining explanations are T132's missing span half and the suite's own
A LARGE gain is the outcome the design expects and is the one to state most
carefully: it would be a gain from a degraded seed on a small model, and it does
not transfer to the hand-written seed or a capable model. It must also survive
the per-template decomposition above before it is reported as a gain at all.
Neither outcome licenses a sixth registration that moves something else until a

method_debugging: train only. The two test splits have been run under registrations 1, 2 and 4,
and their numbers are in findings.md — so this is not written by someone who has
Nothing in it is chosen on one. The suite repair is a defect fix driven by a
property of the generator; the metaprompt fix is driven by a candidate's text
and not by its score; the teacher is chosen on that same candidate's fabricated
schema; the budget is chosen on an iteration count visible in the search log
reporting: Both arms on all three splits, whatever the numbers are, labelled a weak-student
headroom experiment wherever they appear. Neither arm's absolute score is quoted
§7's repeat condition applies unchanged: residual failure counts diverging
between arms mean the arms were not measured under the same conditions and the
run is repeated. Diverging newly-recorded cache entry counts are reported and
stopping: The measurement is complete when both arms have three repeats on all three
splits. It is not stopped early on a favourable interval and not extended on an
unfavourable one. One search, one measurement, one report.

known_gaps.what: The reflective dataset reaches GEPA without its span half: MLflow stands down from tracing when ADK is already tracing, so the search reflects on `Feedback.rationale` and the inputs, not on the ADK tool spans.
known_gaps.status: NOT FIXED. Declared rather than waited for, as in registrations 2, 3 and 4.
known_gaps.effect: The proposer sees less about a rollout than the design intends. It bounds a null here harder than in any earlier run, because the whole point of a stronger proposer is its ability to reason about what went wrong — and it is reasoning from rationales alone.

known_gaps.what: The proposer is asked to rewrite, not to revise, and nothing checks a candidate naming a callable no toolset resolves.
known_gaps.status: NOT FIXED. Checked by hand, as in registrations 3 and 4.
known_gaps.effect: Both earlier winners were checked and both were CLEAN — each named `agent_tool_text_to_sql_agent` only in a sentence forbidding its use, which is T136's seed-side sentence working, reproduced across two different proposers. The same check runs on this run's winner and is reported in findings.md.

known_gaps.what: The answer-leakage check matches literal values and cannot see an answer encoded in words.
known_gaps.status: ACCEPTED. A verbatim match is what registration 4's failure actually was.
known_gaps.effect: A candidate stating `ten percent` rather than `10.0` would pass. The check lowers the probability of an undetected leak; it does not eliminate it, and the per-template decomposition above is the second line of defence.

known_gaps.what: The root agent is an 8B model while the frozen text-to-SQL chain it delegates to is a capable one.
known_gaps.effect: The system under test is not uniformly weak, so this run understates how badly a fully-8B assistant would do. It measures what an 8B ROUTER does with capable tools, which is the quantity the optimizable surface addresses.

known_gaps.what: glm-5.3 is not a dated snapshot, unlike the student and the SQL chain.
known_gaps.status: ACCEPTED and pinned by canary alone.
known_gaps.effect: A provider-side swap under the proposer is detectable only after the fact, on the next run that exercises the canary. It moves what was proposed while leaving every measured surface of the agent untouched, which is §5's stated reason for pinning the reflection model at all.

known_gaps.what: test_unseen lost about 39% of its rollouts in both arms of registrations 2 and 4 to `upstream` cache misses, on a split of seven templates.
known_gaps.effect: test_unseen supports description and not inference, which §7 already required of it.

what: models.served_by: 'gmicloud,mistral,z-ai' -> 'ministral=mistral,deepseek=gmicloud,glm=z-ai'.
The provider pin becomes a per-model mapping rather than a flat whitelist, and
`openrouter_provider_kwargs` takes the model it is pinning. Every call site now
passes its own model id.
`_model_pin` and `reflection_model_pin` record the provider the MODEL resolves
to, rather than the raw setting and `provider[0]` respectively.
`check_pins` verifies the singleton property per model instead of over a global
whitelist. `eval/pins.json` is rewritten: five served_by slots move.
NOTHING ELSE. The budget, the arms, the splits, the repeats, the suite, the
seed, the metaprompt digest, the models themselves and the whole analysis
section are unchanged.
why: THE REGISTERED SEARCH RAN WITH AN EFFECTIVELY UNPINNED PROPOSER, and this
records it rather than discovering it later.
When registration 5 was written, z-ai/glm-5.3 had exactly ONE OpenRouter
provider (`z-ai`), which is why a flat whitelist was sufficient and was
verified as such: the intersection of {gmicloud, mistral, z-ai} with each
model's provider set was a singleton for all three. By the following morning
glm-5.3 was served by SEVEN providers including gmicloud, so the whitelist
admitted both gmicloud and z-ai for that model and OpenRouter was free to route
the reflection calls between them call by call.
That is §5's provider-swap hazard occurring inside a registered run, which is
the hazard T134 introduced the pin to close — and it was closed for the two
models that matter to the numbers and open for the one that does not.
A flat whitelist CANNOT express what this run needs, which is why the fix is a
mechanism change rather than a different list: gmicloud serves both
deepseek-v4-flash and glm-5.3, so no single list pins each of them to one
server. The entries are scoped per model.
The defect was caught by the check written for exactly this in T143 — it failed
the suite the first time it was run after the provider set moved. What it shows
is that the check has to run BEFORE every registered run rather than whenever a
session happens to invoke it, because a provider set can move overnight.
cost: THE T145 SEARCH IS NOT RE-RUN. Its 37 reflection calls may have been split
across gmicloud and z-ai and the logs do not record which served each one: the
provider header is captured for rollouts, through the ledger's witness, and not
for reflection calls. So the candidate this run measures was proposed under a
model whose serving build is unknown, and the search is NOT exactly reproducible.
What is unaffected is every measured number. The measurement never calls the
reflection model; the student and the frozen SQL chain were hard-pinned
throughout and are verified so again after this amendment. The candidate is the
one the search selected, and it is measured as it stands.
Re-running the search would buy exact reproducibility of the proposal step at
~6 hours and EUR 2.76, and would produce a DIFFERENT candidate, which is its own
loss: the run would then report a candidate nobody has examined in place of one
whose text is already recorded in findings.md. The trade is taken deliberately
and the un-reproducibility is stated rather than repaired.
A future run gets both, since the mechanism is fixed from here on.

what: measurement.response_cache_mode: 'replay' -> 'gr2l:replay,weather:record'.
The weather half of the response cache is re-keyed from the WINDOW to the
calendar DAY, and a window is assembled from days. `eval/cache/`'s 1677
committed Open-Meteo window entries were re-keyed in place into 439 day
entries by `scripts/rekey_weather_cache.py`; 11 further days were captured so
that the +/-16-day band around every case's `as_of` is complete. GR2L is
untouched: still keyed on `data[]` plus its parameters, still strict replay on
this path, still an `upstream` exclusion on a miss.
On the measurement path the weather half may now FILL AND RECORD a day it
does not hold, where before a miss excluded the case. The count of entries
recorded is logged per condition (`recorded_entries`) and read beside the
per-arm exclusion count, which is the accounting section 7 already required of
the search.
The capture pass warms a day band rather than a window sweep, which closes the
backward axis it never reached (T25's `past_days=1` route).
NOTHING ELSE. The arms, the splits, the repeats, the suite, the models, the
budget, the seed candidate, the metaprompt digest, the selection weights, the
capture neighbourhood and the whole analysis section are unchanged.
why: THE EXCLUSION RATE THIS RUN IS SUPPOSED TO READ WAS A PROPERTY OF THE CACHE
KEY, NOT OF THE CANDIDATES. Registration 5's search lost 160 of 336
test_unseen rollouts and 116 of 750 test_seen rollouts, every one `upstream`,
and the loss was not spread over the suite: T22 94%, T18b 88%, T26 67%, T23
62%, T21 73%, T09 57% — and T17b zero. The split is between window KINDS. An
absolute past window resolves to one request and hits; a relative forward
window resolves to whichever window the candidate chose, and the cache was
keyed on the request.
One miss cost the CASE and not the call: an excluded case averaged 5.45 extra
tool calls against 0.73 for an included one, 38% hit the step cap and 40% ended
in a `parse_failure`.
Widening the capture neighbourhood cannot fix it and is not being widened. A
window has two degrees of freedom and may be reached through past_days /
forecast_days instead of dates, so the covered set is a line through a plane —
289 windows per `as_of` against 33 days. There is no locality for a wider
neighbourhood to exploit.
Section 5 already licenses it in so many words: what the cache is load-bearing
for is GR2L; for weather it is cost and speed, Archive being re-fetchable
indefinitely. So the component whose determinism the cache carries keeps the
strict rule and the one whose does not stops paying for it.
The re-key is lossless and was verified as such rather than assumed: the 1677
windows agree on all 439 days they overlap on with ZERO conflicts, the 187
entries that were already one day long re-derive byte-identical, and
`scripts/capture_cache.py --verify` replays all 281 cases from the re-keyed
cache with the network blocked and zero live calls.
cost: THE MEASUREMENT PATH IS NO LONGER OFFLINE BY CONSTRUCTION. It replays every
weather day the band holds — measured complete for all 176 distinct `as_of`
days at +/-16 — but a candidate resolving a window outside that band reaches
Open-Meteo during a measured condition. What that buys is the case; what it
costs is that an Open-Meteo outage during the run becomes an exclusion where
it would previously have been a replay. Both are counted and published per
arm, and diverging failure counts still mean the run is repeated.
A weather answer is therefore no longer guaranteed to be byte-identical
between two runs of the same case months apart, where the day was recorded in
between. ERA5 is a reanalysis and its published days do not move, which is why
section 5 never rested a reproducibility claim on this half — but the
guarantee is now the reanalysis's rather than the repository's.
The exclusion counts of registration 5 are NOT comparable with registrations
1-4's on the weather families, since what used to exclude now records. The
GR2L half of the count is unchanged and is comparable.
not_amended: The arms, the splits, the repeats, the pairing, the bootstrap unit and its
seed, the two gaps, the win/loss table, the exclusion RULE (an `upstream`
error still excludes; there is simply one fewer way to produce one), the
diagnostics, the capture neighbourhood, the selection weights, the search
budget and its result, the budget limit, the suite, the seed candidate, the
metaprompt digest, the models, and the whole analysis and protocol sections.
